DopMenu Privacy policy Support

Support

DopMenu is a timer for the Mac menu bar. Choose how much time and energy you have, pick something that fits, and DopMenu times it. It needs macOS 26 or later.

Contact

Write to dopmenu.app@gmail.com. It helps to include:

  • your macOS version (Apple menu → About This Mac)
  • the DopMenu version, on the last line of its Settings
  • what you did, what you expected, and what happened

Your email is handled as the privacy policy says.

Getting started

DopMenu lives in the menu bar: click the bolt to open the panel, click it again or anywhere else to close it. Closing the panel never stops a timer.

The idea: when you have a gap, tell the app how much time and energy you have, and it shows only what fits. Pick one, start the timer, and press Did it when you have done it.

  • Can't see the bolt? Press Control-Option-Command-D from anywhere. See “The icon is hidden”.

Time and energy

Time is how long you have: 5, 15 or 25 minutes. Energy is how you feel: Low, Medium or High.

The list shows activities that need no more than that time and that energy. The number above the list says how many fit.

The time you choose is the length of the timer. A 5-minute activity started with 25 minutes chosen runs for 25 minutes.

Starting and stopping

Click a row to start its timer. The bolt in the menu bar shows the time left.

  • Pause and Resume keep the time exactly where it was.
  • Stop ends the session; nothing is counted as done.
  • Starting another activity while one runs asks first: Replace, or Cancel to keep the current one.

The timer keeps going when the panel is closed, when the Mac sleeps, and when you quit and reopen the app.

When the time is up

Three gentle notes play and a notification says “Session finished”. The panel does not open by itself.

In the panel you then choose: Did it (counts it), Start again (same length), or × (nothing counted).

Nothing is ever counted automatically: only Did it counts.

Did it, Undo and your week

Did it marks an activity done, whether you used the timer or not. The row leaves the list until tomorrow.

Pressed it by mistake? Click Undo on the message at the bottom, or open Manage activities later: everything done today is listed there with its own Undo.

“N done this week” counts every Did it since Monday 00:00.

Click “N done this week” at the top of the panel to see what you did today, each with the time you pressed Did it; “See the whole week…” opens Manage activities, where the earlier days of this week are listed day by day.

Several times a day

Some things are worth doing more than once: water, stretching, a short walk. Open the activity’s editor (⋯ → Edit activity) and set TIMES A DAY to 2–5.

The row then stays in the list with “1/3 today”, and leaves after the last one.

A quick double-click counts once.

Just pick one for me

Can’t decide? This picks one of the activities that fit and starts it. It avoids the one it picked last time.

If nothing fits, it says so: loosen a filter or add something small.

Your activities

  • Add your own: type a name and press Return. It uses the time and energy chosen now.
  • ⋯ on a row: Edit activity, Snooze for today, Stop timer, Remove activity.
  • Snooze hides an activity until tomorrow.
  • Remove asks first. What you already did with it still counts; Undo brings it back.
  • Manage activities (bottom of the panel) lists everything, including what is done or snoozed today.
  • If DopMenu asked you five questions when it first opened, Tailor your list… in Manage activities lets you change the answers: a new yes adds its activities, a new no asks before removing any.

The icon is hidden

On a MacBook with a camera notch, a full menu bar can push the bolt behind the notch.

  • Press Control-Option-Command-D from anywhere to open the panel.
  • Open the app again from Spotlight or Applications: the panel opens.
  • Settings → Compact menu bar icon shows only the bolt, which needs less room.
  • To move the bolt: hold Command and drag it to the right in the menu bar.

Settings

Click the gear at the top of the panel.

  • Notifications: allow the “Session finished” banner. If macOS blocks it, Open takes you to the switch.
  • Completion chime: the three notes on or off.
  • Launch at login: macOS may ask you to approve it in System Settings → General → Login Items.
  • Appearance: System, Light or Dark.

Using the keyboard

Turn on System Settings → Keyboard → Keyboard navigation, then:

  • Tab moves between controls; ← and → change Time and Energy.
  • Space or Return presses the control with the ring.
  • Escape closes the top-most thing first (a question, the editor, Settings, the “How it works” card, the today list, Add your own), then the panel.

Your data

Everything stays on this Mac, in the app's own folder, which macOS keeps for it alone. Your list and history are in ~/Library/Containers/com.romane002.DopamineMenu/Data/Library/Application Support/Dopamine Menu/state.json, with a backup copy beside it. Nothing is sent anywhere; the app never uses the internet.

If a save ever fails, a card says so, your last saved state stays safe, and Try again saves now.

Each Mac keeps its own list; there is no syncing.

Privacy

DopMenu collects no data, and what it keeps stays on your Mac. See the privacy policy.

Removing DopMenu

To remove DopMenu and everything it has kept on your Mac, follow Deleting your data in the privacy policy.
